name: WI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Scott Fitzgerald with $1.3M war chest vs. $3K for Beck
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Fitzgerald's massive financial advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win at just 2% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. No evidence suggests Beck can close a double-digit structural gap.
model.watch: A major scandal or a sharply unfavorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Fitzgerald, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this suburban Milwaukee district that leans Republican by about 11 points. He has raised over $1.3 million and holds a dominant cash advantage, while Democratic challenger Andrew Beck has raised only about $15,000. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 2% chance of an upset.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided fundraising gap. A Republican win is expected by a wide margin, though not with the certainty of a race where no major-party challenger is on the ballot.
